title: Dangers from outer space
paragraphs: What is the greatest threat to life on our planet? Is it climate change? Is it a shortage of food or water? Or could a bigger danger come from further afield: from space?

We're not talking about an invasion by little green men here. Instead, how about the prospect of being hit by a gigantic meteorite, zapped by lethal cosmic rays or fried by the deadly energy of an erupting star?

It wouldn't be the first time. Good old planet Earth has had a rough ride over the last 3.7 billion years, with some spectacularly devastating events. The most famous mass extinction was 66 million years ago, when it's widely believed a meteorite killed off the dinosaurs. A 110-mile-wide crater in Mexico with the same geological age supports this theory.

Believe it or not, this wasn't the most brutal episode in our planet's history. That was when a staggering 96% of life was wiped out at the end of the Permian period, 252 million years ago. Scientists don't know for sure why this happened, but any potential explanations carry with them the grim possibility that similar events could happen again.

For example, some experts believe that our Sun has a very dense, dim twin star which is too far away to observe directly. This sleeping giant, dubbed the "Death Star", could distort the paths of orbiting chunks of icy rock and hurl them towards the rest of the Solar System.
Is this what happened 252 million years ago? Or is there instead, perhaps, a distant, ninth planet in our Solar System which pulls in passing comets and sends them hurtling our way?

If that isn't enough to put you off your breakfast, then consider what's happening to our friend, the Sun. The star that has given us the warmth to sustain life is gradually turning into a deadly foe. Like all stars, it is slowly dying, burning through its energy supplies. As it does so, it expands, and in about 2 billion years it will have grown so much that the heat will make life on planet Earth unbearable.
While all this sounds a little macabre, take comfort from the fact that the chance of being hit by a giant interstellar projectile is incredibly slim, and that 2 billion years is a very long time.
And there's another thing: if the dinosaurs had not snuffed it when they did, it's extremely unlikely that human beings would have had the chance to evolve at all.

vocabulary.entry: meteorite [n.] /ˈmiːtiəraɪt/ 陨石
vocabulary.example: A large meteorite struck the Earth millions of years ago.
vocabulary.translation: 数百万年前一颗巨大的陨石撞击了地球。

vocabulary.entry: zap [v.] /zæp/ 击中；摧毁 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The lightning zapped the tree.
vocabulary.translation: 闪电击中了那棵树。

vocabulary.entry: lethal [adj.] /ˈliːθəl/ 致命的
vocabulary.example: The snake's venom is lethal to humans.
vocabulary.translation: 这种蛇的毒液对人类是致命的。

vocabulary.entry: cosmic rays [n. pl.] /ˈkɒzmɪk reɪz/ 宇宙射线 (单数: cosmic ray)
vocabulary.example: Cosmic rays come from outer space.
vocabulary.translation: 宇宙射线来自外太空。

vocabulary.entry: erupting star [n.] /ɪˈrʌptɪŋ stɑː/ 爆发中的恒星
vocabulary.example: Scientists study the energy released by erupting stars.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家研究爆发中的恒星释放的能量。

vocabulary.entry: a rough ride [phr.] /ə rʌf raɪd/ 艰难的历程
vocabulary.example: The company has had a rough ride this year.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司今年经历了一段艰难的时期。

vocabulary.entry: devastating [adj.] /ˈdevəsteɪtɪŋ/ 毁灭性的
vocabulary.example: The earthquake had devastating effects on the city.
vocabulary.translation: 地震给这座城市带来了毁灭性的影响。

vocabulary.entry: mass extinction [n.] /ˌmæs ɪkˈstɪŋkʃən/ 大规模灭绝 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The extinction of the dinosaurs was a mass extinction event.
vocabulary.translation: 恐龙的灭绝是一次大规模灭绝事件。

vocabulary.entry: kill off [phr.] /kɪl ɒf/ 消灭；使灭绝
vocabulary.example: The disease killed off most of the population.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病消灭了大部分人口。

vocabulary.entry: crater [n.] /ˈkreɪtə/ 陨石坑；火山口
vocabulary.example: The meteorite left a huge crater in the ground.
vocabulary.translation: 陨石在地面上留下了一个巨大的坑。

vocabulary.entry: geological [adj.] /ˌdʒiːəˈlɒdʒɪkəl/ 地质的
vocabulary.example: Geological studies help us understand Earth's history.
vocabulary.translation: 地质研究帮助我们了解地球的历史。

vocabulary.entry: brutal [adj.] /ˈbruːtəl/ 残酷的；野蛮的
vocabulary.example: The war was brutal and lasted for years.
vocabulary.translation: 这场战争很残酷，持续了多年。

vocabulary.entry: episode [n.] /ˈepɪsəʊd/ 事件；时期
vocabulary.example: That was a dark episode in the country's history.
vocabulary.translation: 那是该国历史上的一个黑暗时期。

vocabulary.entry: staggering [adj.] /ˈstæɡərɪŋ/ 惊人的；令人震惊的
vocabulary.example: The cost of the project is staggering.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的成本惊人。

vocabulary.entry: wiped out [phr.] /waɪpt aʊt/ 消灭；彻底摧毁
vocabulary.example: The entire village was wiped out by the flood.
vocabulary.translation: 整个村庄被洪水摧毁了。

vocabulary.entry: for sure [phr.] /fə ʃʊə/ 确实；肯定
vocabulary.example: I don't know for sure what happened.
vocabulary.translation: 我不确定发生了什么。

vocabulary.entry: grim [adj.] /ɡrɪm/ 严峻的；令人沮丧的
vocabulary.example: The outlook for the future is grim.
vocabulary.translation: 未来的前景很严峻。

vocabulary.entry: carry with [phr.] /ˈkæri wɪð/ 伴随；带有
vocabulary.example: This decision carries with it serious consequences.
vocabulary.translation: 这个决定伴随着严重的后果。

vocabulary.entry: dense [adj.] /dens/ 致密的；密度大的

vocabulary.translation: 这颗行星有稠密的大气层。

vocabulary.entry: distort [v.] /dɪˈstɔːt/ 扭曲；变形

vocabulary.translation: 镜子扭曲了他的映像。

vocabulary.example: The hurtling comet was visible in the night sky.
vocabulary.translation: 那颗飞驰的彗星在夜空中可见。

vocabulary.entry: put off [phr.] /pʊt ɒf/ 使反感；使失去兴趣
vocabulary.example: The smell put me off my food.
vocabulary.translation: 这股气味让我没了食欲。

vocabulary.entry: sustain [v.] /səˈsteɪn/ 维持；保持
vocabulary.example: The planet cannot sustain this level of pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 地球无法维持这种程度的污染。

vocabulary.entry: foe [n.] /fəʊ/ 敌人
vocabulary.example: In the movie, the hero fights his foe.
vocabulary.translation: 电影中，英雄与他的敌人战斗。

vocabulary.entry: macabre [adj.] /məˈkɑːbrə/ 可怕的；令人毛骨悚然的
vocabulary.example: The film has a macabre sense of humour.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有一种令人毛骨悚然的幽默感。

vocabulary.entry: take comfort from [phr.] /teɪk ˈkʌmfət frɒm/ 从……中得到安慰
vocabulary.example: She took comfort from her friends' support.
vocabulary.translation: 她从朋友们的支持中得到了安慰。

vocabulary.entry: interstellar [adj.] /ˌɪntəˈstelə/ 星际的
vocabulary.example: Interstellar travel is still science fiction.
vocabulary.translation: 星际旅行仍是科幻小说。

vocabulary.entry: projectile [n.] /prəˈdʒektaɪl/ 抛射物；射弹
vocabulary.example: The meteorite was a projectile from space.
vocabulary.translation: 这颗陨石是来自太空的抛射物。

vocabulary.entry: incredibly [adv.] /ɪnˈkredəbli/ 极其；难以置信地
vocabulary.example: The chance of winning is incredibly small.
vocabulary.translation: 获胜的几率极其渺茫。

vocabulary.entry: snuff it [phr.] /snʌf ɪt/ 死去；一命呜呼 (英式口语；俚语)
vocabulary.example: The old horse finally snuffed it.
vocabulary.translation: 那匹老马最终还是死了。

sentences.english: It wouldn't be the first time.
sentences.chinese: 这可不是第一次了。

sentences.english: That was when a staggering 96% of life was wiped out at the end of the Permian period, 252 million years ago.
sentences.chinese: 最残酷的是在2.52亿年前的二叠纪末期，惊人的96%的生命灭绝了。

sentences.chinese: 科学家们不确定这是为什么，但任何可能的解释都伴随着类似事件可能再次发生的令人沮丧的可能性。

sentences.english: For example, some experts believe that our Sun has a very dense, dim twin star which is too far away to observe directly.
sentences.chinese: 例如，一些专家认为我们的太阳有一颗非常致密、昏暗的伴星，它距离太远，无法直接观测到。

sentences.english: This sleeping giant, dubbed the "Death Star", could distort the paths of orbiting chunks of icy rock and hurl them towards the rest of the Solar System.
sentences.chinese: 这个被称为“死亡之星”的沉睡巨人，可能会扭曲绕轨道运行的冰岩块的路径，并将它们抛向太阳系的其他地方。

sentences.english: Is this what happened 252 million years ago?
sentences.chinese: 这就是2.52亿年前发生的事情吗？

sentences.english: Or is there instead, perhaps, a distant, ninth planet in our Solar System which pulls in passing comets and sends them hurtling our way?
sentences.chinese: 或者，也许在我们的太阳系中有一颗遥远的第九颗行星，它吸引路过的彗星，并将它们朝着我们的方向猛冲过来？

sentences.chinese: 如果这还不足以让你没了吃早餐的胃口，那就想想我们的朋友——太阳正在发生什么吧。
